content: \n								The way you design the layout of your museum, how you organize the exhibits and how you decorate them have a meaningful impact on the success of your museum. This already makes it a better game than Two Point Hospital and Two Point Campus. It's also a lot of fun to do!I also love how you progress in this game. There's a limitation on how many stars you can achieve in a map at the beginning, and you'll have to progress through objectives by playing other maps. Afterwards, you can (and have to) return to previous maps to achieve new stars by completing a new set of objectives. This way you'll be going back and forth between maps you already played, instead of playing a map until you achieve 3 stars and then abandon it completely, like in the previous Two Point games.The different categories of museums make the game quite diverse. For example, the Prehistoric category is mostly about digging up exhibits and displaying the best ones in your museum, while the Science category is all about building your own science exhibits and upgrading them by completing challenges. There's also a bit of synergy between categories, so for example you'll be running a Science museum that also has a Botany section.Expeditions can be challenging, but can also become a bit of a grind, especially when you're after the pristine quality exhibits. Exhibits are chance-based drops, although you can significantly increase your chances of getting a pristine quality item with various things such as the survey scanner and specific skills and traits of your experts and staff.The biggest weak point of this game is its security mechanic. From time to time, thieves and vandals will come to your museum disguised as normal guests. You'll have to employ security guards and place cameras to expose and catch them. This sounds like a fun challenge, but in reality it's only an annoying distraction and the security guards are quite stupid. For example, they won't work together to catch a thief, only one guard at a time will be chasing after a thief. Often, a thief can do their thing even with a guard present next to the thief, just because the thief is slightly out of the guard's field of vision. When a lot of thieves are active in a map, you'll be constantly pausing the game and dragging security guards to thieves to catch them. I give this game a big thumbs-up! Running a museum sounds like the most boring thing in the world, but Two Point Studios managed to make this a lot of fun!

content: \n								The way you design the layout of your museum, how you organize the exhibits and how you decorate them have a meaningful impact on the success of your museum. This already makes it a better game than Two Point Hospital and Two Point Campus. It's also a lot of fun to do!I also love how you progress in this game. There's a limitation on how many stars you can achieve in a map at the beginning, and you'll have to progress through objectives by playing other maps. Afterwards, you can (and have to) return to previous maps to achieve new stars by completing a new set of objectives. This way you'll be going back and forth between maps you already played, instead of playing a map until you achieve 3 stars and then abandon it completely, like in the previous Two Point games.The different categories of museums make the game quite diverse. For example, the Prehistoric category is mostly about digging up exhibits and displaying the best ones in your museum, while the Science category is all about building your own science exhibits and upgrading them by completing challenges. There's also a bit of synergy between categories, so for example you'll be running a Science museum that also has a Botany section.Expeditions can be challenging, but can also become a bit of a grind, especially when you're after the pristine quality exhibits. Exhibits are chance-based drops, although you can significantly increase your chances of getting a pristine quality item with various things such as the survey scanner and specific skills and traits of your experts and staff.The biggest weak point of this game is its security mechanic. From time to time, thieves and vandals will come to your museum disguised as normal guests. You'll have to employ security guards and place cameras to expose and catch them. This sounds like a fun challenge, but in reality it's only an annoying distraction and the security guards are quite stupid. For example, they won't work together to catch a thief, only one guard at a time will be chasing after a thief. Often, a thief can do their thing even with a guard present next to the thief, just because the thief is slightly out of the guard's field of vision. When a lot of thieves are active in a map, you'll be constantly pausing the game and dragging security guards to thieves to catch them. I give this game a big thumbs-up! Running a museum sounds like the most boring thing in the world, but Two Point Studios managed to make this a lot of fun!

content: \n								The way you design the layout of your museum, how you organize the exhibits and how you decorate them have a meaningful impact on the success of your museum. This already makes it a better game than Two Point Hospital and Two Point Campus. It's also a lot of fun to do!I also love how you progress in this game. There's a limitation on how many stars you can achieve in a map at the beginning, and you'll have to progress through objectives by playing other maps. Afterwards, you can (and have to) return to previous maps to achieve new stars by completing a new set of objectives. This way you'll be going back and forth between maps you already played, instead of playing a map until you achieve 3 stars and then abandon it completely, like in the previous Two Point games.The different categories of museums make the game quite diverse. For example, the Prehistoric category is mostly about digging up exhibits and displaying the best ones in your museum, while the Science category is all about building your own science exhibits and upgrading them by completing challenges. There's also a bit of synergy between categories, so for example you'll be running a Science museum that also has a Botany section.Expeditions can be challenging, but can also become a bit of a grind, especially when you're after the pristine quality exhibits. Exhibits are chance-based drops, although you can significantly increase your chances of getting a pristine quality item with various things such as the survey scanner and specific skills and traits of your experts and staff.The biggest weak point of this game is its security mechanic. From time to time, thieves and vandals will come to your museum disguised as normal guests. You'll have to employ security guards and place cameras to expose and catch them. This sounds like a fun challenge, but in reality it's only an annoying distraction and the security guards are quite stupid. For example, they won't work together to catch a thief, only one guard at a time will be chasing after a thief. Often, a thief can do their thing even with a guard present next to the thief, just because the thief is slightly out of the guard's field of vision. When a lot of thieves are active in a map, you'll be constantly pausing the game and dragging security guards to thieves to catch them. I give this game a big thumbs-up! Running a museum sounds like the most boring thing in the world, but Two Point Studios managed to make this a lot of fun!

content: \n								Having put 100 hours into Two Point Hospital over two Steam accounts and around 50-60 in Campus, I was very skeptical of the theme of this game when it was announced. I figured that the game play style Two Point is used to would never work for a Museum game, but I can say without a doubt I was very wrong.The game play loop of this game is definitely different than the other two games. You don't have 1 person or a small group of people you watch over as they fulfill one single task. Instead, every guest is different and wants their own things to make them happy. On top of this, collecting your exhibits is incredibly fun and I honestly love the gamble style loot box-esque game play of getting these exhibits. It forces you to think about how you upgrade your staff so you can maximize your searches and save your staff from injury. Really my only problem with the game is that they don't emphasize enough your possible money making tactics. I knew the gift shop made me money, but I figured it wasnt enough to warrant the space and staff I'd have to spend. Now in the late game I make insane money off of it.---All in all, this is definitely my favorite game in the Two Point series and I can't wait for the DLC's when they come around.

There's a lot more creative expression here, and it was sorely missing from previous instalments. I'm scared for what the future of the DLC will bring as I've always found TP DLC to be rather half-baked, but we'll see. With the improvements to TPM, I am holding some hope that the DLC won't just be cash-grabs.

I still haven't even filled the original building.... found this odd Workshop, wasn't aware you could make cargo items, again was never mentioned ..... Also, would be nice to know if certain rooms like the training room etc have new items that have been unlocked and are  ready to be placed. I had no idea you could unlock diplomas on the wall to reduce time etc...The health inspector will come and (I assume) go through your trash to make sure they are not full? and that no trash is on the floor. Well no trash is ever on my floor and I have no way of knowing if a trash can is full unless I look at it..... Most of the time the report from the health inspector comes back "trash visible cans full" yet I have no issues with the museum rating etc.....Zones are completely broken for me. content: \n								This may be the most fun I've ever had in a management game! So far Two Point Museum, despite me only having played it for around 5 hours at them moment, has had me looking forward to my time with it each day. It's very well put together, as is the tutorial. The idea of sending people out on expeditions to find the bits for your museum is genius! It gives you a little excitement as to what's going to happen and what you are going to discover next. It also adds an extra element when your explorers come back caked in mud and walk it through your museum. The game has had me laughing at the npcs and some of the names of artifacts. The radio is also quite funny. The decoration and management aspects have been easy to get to grips with so far whilst also being deep and interesting. content: \n								I work in museums, so I had "opinions" when this was announced, shortly followed by an obsessive desire to pre-order it. I have wanted a museum game for nearly a decade, and I am so pleased that Two Point studios picked up the challenge. The result is Two Point Museum, a game that presents museum as I would like them to be: an exciting and vibrant place, where learning and fun go hand in hand. Oh, and it's also a very solid, if a little relaxed, management game, you know, in case you cared about that too.I could wax lyrical about the aesthetic of the Two Point universe for days, and it's no different in Museum. The voice acting on the radio is excellent: charming and not too repetitive. The music is lovely and relaxing. The jokes all land, both the quite clever history jokes, and the more obvious puns. If you've played a Two Point game, you know what you're in for and if you haven't you'll love it. The museums, guests, and exhibits, are full of personality, and it draws you into just sitting and watching people go round the museum, and enjoying themselves. Interestingly though, I haven't able or willing to do that often, because the management aspect of this game is so engrossing.There is always something going on in a Two Point Museum. There's expeditions to do to get more exhibits, staff to manage, guests to keep happy, criminals to catch, and, if you're me, lots of decorating. You're constantly bouncing from one job to the next, and there's very few times I was just sitting around waiting for the next expedition to finish. Both campaign and sandbox helps with this by forcing you to switch between five different main museums each with their own themes, and three "pop-up museums" that act as the game's challenge levels. You never get comfortable for very long, and the campaign does do a great job of layering mechanics as you progress. In fact, the whole game is very accessible. Moving objects, and building rooms, is really easy, and there's a great variety to build too. There's a real sense of discovery and learning as you progress, and in a game about museums, that's what you want.I love it, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't have several gripes with it. There are bugs, nothing gamebreaking, and nothing glaringly obvious, but those that are there are annoying: rewards not getting unlocked, museum staff getting stuck for no obvious reason, cutscene sounds occasionally not triggering etc. I do think there could be more exhibit themed wallpapers and floors, but it says something of the game's quality that the biggest gameplay issue I have is with litter. Litter is often too small to spot in busy areas, and has no system or lense to monitor it, making it a very difficult problem to solve accurately without flooding your museum with bins and janitors. A slightly larger "concern" is that I didn't find the game to be very challenging and I've never been in a situation that put me in great difficulty. Sure, exhibits got stolen, and I did overspend on expeditions more than once, but everything was recoverable, and the pop-up museums are trivialised with the use of loans to get you started financially. It might be my slow style of play, and to be fair I don't think this detracts from enjoying the game, but I feel that those who want a difficult management puzzle should look elsewhere.In fact, my biggest complaint about Two Point Museum? I want more of it! I don't want to stop playing it. It's baffling to be in that position considering I've already played 40 hours, but I can't help it. Two Point Museum is a fantastic game. For less than half the price of a AAA game you get a brilliant, quirky, management sim, that manages to delight and engage in equal measure. I cannot wait to see what other things the developers have in store. It's such a good game, one might even say it belongs in a museum.

I have wanted a museum game for nearly a decade, and I am so pleased that Two Point studios picked up the challenge. The result is Two Point Museum, a game that presents museum as I would like them to be: an exciting and vibrant place, where learning and fun go hand in hand. Oh, and it's also a very solid, if a little relaxed, management game, you know, in case you cared about that too.I could wax lyrical about the aesthetic of the Two Point universe for days, and it's no different in Museum. The voice acting on the radio is excellent: charming and not too repetitive. The music is lovely and relaxing. The jokes all land, both the quite clever history jokes, and the more obvious puns. If you've played a Two Point game, you know what you're in for and if you haven't you'll love it. The museums, guests, and exhibits, are full of personality, and it draws you into just sitting and watching people go round the museum, and enjoying themselves. Interestingly though, I haven't able or willing to do that often, because the management aspect of this game is so engrossing.There is always something going on in a Two Point Museum. There's expeditions to do to get more exhibits, staff to manage, guests to keep happy, criminals to catch, and, if you're me, lots of decorating. You're constantly bouncing from one job to the next, and there's very few times I was just sitting around waiting for the next expedition to finish. Both campaign and sandbox helps with this by forcing you to switch between five different main museums each with their own themes, and three "pop-up museums" that act as the game's challenge levels. You never get comfortable for very long, and the campaign does do a great job of layering mechanics as you progress. In fact, the whole game is very accessible. Moving objects, and building rooms, is really easy, and there's a great variety to build too. There's a real sense of discovery and learning as you progress, and in a game about museums, that's what you want.I love it, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't have several gripes with it. There are bugs, nothing gamebreaking, and nothing glaringly obvious, but those that are there are annoying: rewards not getting unlocked, museum staff getting stuck for no obvious reason, cutscene sounds occasionally not triggering etc. I do think there could be more exhibit themed wallpapers and floors, but it says something of the game's quality that the biggest gameplay issue I have is with litter. Litter is often too small to spot in busy areas, and has no system or lense to monitor it, making it a very difficult problem to solve accurately without flooding your museum with bins and janitors. A slightly larger "concern" is that I didn't find the game to be very challenging and I've never been in a situation that put me in great difficulty. Sure, exhibits got stolen, and I did overspend on expeditions more than once, but everything was recoverable, and the pop-up museums are trivialised with the use of loans to get you started financially. It might be my slow style of play, and to be fair I don't think this detracts from enjoying the game, but I feel that those who want a difficult management puzzle should look elsewhere.In fact, my biggest complaint about Two Point Museum? I want more of it! I don't want to stop playing it. It's baffling to be in that position considering I've already played 40 hours, but I can't help it. Two Point Museum is a fantastic game. For less than half the price of a AAA game you get a brilliant, quirky, management sim, that manages to delight and engage in equal measure. I cannot wait to see what other things the developers have in store. It's such a good game, one might even say it belongs in a museum.

content: \n								I work in museums, so I had "opinions" when this was announced, shortly followed by an obsessive desire to pre-order it. I have wanted a museum game for nearly a decade, and I am so pleased that Two Point studios picked up the challenge. The result is Two Point Museum, a game that presents museum as I would like them to be: an exciting and vibrant place, where learning and fun go hand in hand. Oh, and it's also a very solid, if a little relaxed, management game, you know, in case you cared about that too.I could wax lyrical about the aesthetic of the Two Point universe for days, and it's no different in Museum. The voice acting on the radio is excellent: charming and not too repetitive. The music is lovely and relaxing. The jokes all land, both the quite clever history jokes, and the more obvious puns. If you've played a Two Point game, you know what you're in for and if you haven't you'll love it. The museums, guests, and exhibits, are full of personality, and it draws you into just sitting and watching people go round the museum, and enjoying themselves. Interestingly though, I haven't able or willing to do that often, because the management aspect of this game is so engrossing.There is always something going on in a Two Point Museum. There's expeditions to do to get more exhibits, staff to manage, guests to keep happy, criminals to catch, and, if you're me, lots of decorating. You're constantly bouncing from one job to the next, and there's very few times I was just sitting around waiting for the next expedition to finish. Both campaign and sandbox helps with this by forcing you to switch between five different main museums each with their own themes, and three "pop-up museums" that act as the game's challenge levels. You never get comfortable for very long, and the campaign does do a great job of layering mechanics as you progress. In fact, the whole game is very accessible. Moving objects, and building rooms, is really easy, and there's a great variety to build too. There's a real sense of discovery and learning as you progress, and in a game about museums, that's what you want.I love it, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't have several gripes with it. There are bugs, nothing gamebreaking, and nothing glaringly obvious, but those that are there are annoying: rewards not getting unlocked, museum staff getting stuck for no obvious reason, cutscene sounds occasionally not triggering etc. I do think there could be more exhibit themed wallpapers and floors, but it says something of the game's quality that the biggest gameplay issue I have is with litter. Litter is often too small to spot in busy areas, and has no system or lense to monitor it, making it a very difficult problem to solve accurately without flooding your museum with bins and janitors. A slightly larger "concern" is that I didn't find the game to be very challenging and I've never been in a situation that put me in great difficulty. Sure, exhibits got stolen, and I did overspend on expeditions more than once, but everything was recoverable, and the pop-up museums are trivialised with the use of loans to get you started financially. It might be my slow style of play, and to be fair I don't think this detracts from enjoying the game, but I feel that those who want a difficult management puzzle should look elsewhere.In fact, my biggest complaint about Two Point Museum? I want more of it! I don't want to stop playing it. It's baffling to be in that position considering I've already played 40 hours, but I can't help it. Two Point Museum is a fantastic game. For less than half the price of a AAA game you get a brilliant, quirky, management sim, that manages to delight and engage in equal measure. I cannot wait to see what other things the developers have in store. It's such a good game, one might even say it belongs in a museum.

content: \n								I work in museums, so I had "opinions" when this was announced, shortly followed by an obsessive desire to pre-order it. I have wanted a museum game for nearly a decade, and I am so pleased that Two Point studios picked up the challenge. The result is Two Point Museum, a game that presents museum as I would like them to be: an exciting and vibrant place, where learning and fun go hand in hand. Oh, and it's also a very solid, if a little relaxed, management game, you know, in case you cared about that too.I could wax lyrical about the aesthetic of the Two Point universe for days, and it's no different in Museum. The voice acting on the radio is excellent: charming and not too repetitive. The music is lovely and relaxing. The jokes all land, both the quite clever history jokes, and the more obvious puns. If you've played a Two Point game, you know what you're in for and if you haven't you'll love it. The museums, guests, and exhibits, are full of personality, and it draws you into just sitting and watching people go round the museum, and enjoying themselves. Interestingly though, I haven't able or willing to do that often, because the management aspect of this game is so engrossing.There is always something going on in a Two Point Museum. There's expeditions to do to get more exhibits, staff to manage, guests to keep happy, criminals to catch, and, if you're me, lots of decorating. You're constantly bouncing from one job to the next, and there's very few times I was just sitting around waiting for the next expedition to finish. Both campaign and sandbox helps with this by forcing you to switch between five different main museums each with their own themes, and three "pop-up museums" that act as the game's challenge levels. You never get comfortable for very long, and the campaign does do a great job of layering mechanics as you progress. In fact, the whole game is very accessible. Moving objects, and building rooms, is really easy, and there's a great variety to build too. There's a real sense of discovery and learning as you progress, and in a game about museums, that's what you want.I love it, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't have several gripes with it. There are bugs, nothing gamebreaking, and nothing glaringly obvious, but those that are there are annoying: rewards not getting unlocked, museum staff getting stuck for no obvious reason, cutscene sounds occasionally not triggering etc. I do think there could be more exhibit themed wallpapers and floors, but it says something of the game's quality that the biggest gameplay issue I have is with litter. Litter is often too small to spot in busy areas, and has no system or lense to monitor it, making it a very difficult problem to solve accurately without flooding your museum with bins and janitors. A slightly larger "concern" is that I didn't find the game to be very challenging and I've never been in a situation that put me in great difficulty. Sure, exhibits got stolen, and I did overspend on expeditions more than once, but everything was recoverable, and the pop-up museums are trivialised with the use of loans to get you started financially. It might be my slow style of play, and to be fair I don't think this detracts from enjoying the game, but I feel that those who want a difficult management puzzle should look elsewhere.In fact, my biggest complaint about Two Point Museum? I want more of it! I don't want to stop playing it. It's baffling to be in that position considering I've already played 40 hours, but I can't help it. Two Point Museum is a fantastic game. For less than half the price of a AAA game you get a brilliant, quirky, management sim, that manages to delight and engage in equal measure. I cannot wait to see what other things the developers have in store. It's such a good game, one might even say it belongs in a museum.

content: \n								I'm going to be very direct here:Theme Hospital was the very first game I ever bought. It was and STILL is my comfort game, It is my favorite game, it molded my taste in computer games, it's a cherished and beloved part of my life. And it's also the absolute Gold Standard to which I hold every Two Point game in comparison.That said, TP Hospital has a heartwarming life experience of seeing your very best friends from childhood again. Yes they've changed a bit, maybe a bit clunky, but still you love them... (The UI was absolute terrible, but it was an overall good game)TP Campus was a weird twist... It's not a bad game, but the choice of making a university simulator was a bit odd and honestly didn't attract me as much. Although the mechanics and UI were improved, I just couldn't immerse myself in the game, and apparently a lot of people felt the same.With that out of the way:Two Point Museum is BY FAR the absolute best game Two Point Studios have made until now.Not only that, I put this game on the same level as my dear precious Theme Hospital. It's important you understand I don't say this lightly! Theme Hospital is my most cherished game. To me, it's just perfect.Yes, I don't have the same emotional attachment to Two Point Museum as I do with Theme Hospital, and I never will. That won't ever happen again. But still, Two Point Museum is a EXCELLENT game. It's well-made, It's full of mechanics, even though it didn't even get any DLC yet. This game looks and feels like it was created with the most absolute care, by a team that knows what they're doing.I said before, the UI on TP Hospital is absolute ♥♥♥♥. Two Point Museum however NAILED the UI experience on this game. Menus and overall UI are gorgeous and efficient. They fit the game so well.If they released a paid DLC to add the same UI to Two Point Hospital, I'd buy that NOW, and honestly, I hope developers think about it.Above everything else, Two Point Museum is really, really FUN.If you played Theme Hospital, you'll like it.If you played Two Point Hospital, you'll like it.If you played Two Point Campus, you'll like it.If you didn't play ANY of those, you'll probably like it too.If you're on the fence about playing this game, go ahead, It is worth it!!!

content: \n								This game is a great addition to the Two Point franchise and I dropped everything and bought it on release day. It has already because my favorite game of all time - I was a Two Point Hospital and Campus player and those games were very fun. Replayability has always been a concern with the franchise, but TP Museum has actually done a great job of making the game refreshing enough to HAVE to revisit and you can tell developers actually give a crap about the game and its fans. Having now played for just under 50 hours, there are two flaws that I'm sure will get fixed soon:1) After you get 2 stars on the first set of museum sites and you have to get up to 2 more additional stars (making the total 3 stars for 2 hotels). I'm not saying I am playing on a super hefty gaming computer (I'm admittedly on a macbook), but the game becomes essentially unplayable with the amount of lag. This also happens BEFORE you build out your museum, but if you keep the camera zoomed in it is a decent workaround for the time being. However, for $40 the game should be able to handle this. 2) There are some tasks that are contradictory. For instance: There was a polterguest that had two buzz requirements: to provide a water basin, and to provide zero water sources. How exactly would you deal with this, since the water basin is a water source. I threw him in the analyzer, but I feel like this is a slight oversight. It honestly reminded me of Jurassic World Evolution and the lazily designed challenges for dinosaurs. This is NOT good! However, it is rare enough that it hasn't horribly impact game play.Honorable mention) I think the mechanic for the fish is somewhat broken. In aquariums around the world, you have sharks with fish, starfish, sealions, etc., and I think it might be worth revisiting the lion head fish, the tiger shark, etc., because they wind up needing their own aquarium which, if the progression of the campaign is followed, is just not worth it to have all the fish. I get wanting to be selective, but this just seems needlessly silly and detracts from the overall feature. Also, this might just be luck of the draw, but I have explored lion head fish 1000 times and I still have never gotten a pristine/epic lion head fish. Anyways, it is 100% worth the price and I think the explorer edition is worth the extra $10 just in time saving and additional features. If you are like me and grew up going to a museum as a kid, this is the game for you. It keeps the humourous charm of the first two games and I love the thoughtfulness that the developers put it into it. Highly recommend, and will recommend even more if the lag issues get fixed.

content: \n Not Two Point, but Seven Point Zero  What I Liked Never thought making a museum game would work, but it certainly does.  Place exhibits, tend to them, find new exhibits, cater to guests, all that.  It works decently well.While I didn't get too far, my favorite type of museum is the supernatural.  The look, the exhibits, everything about it is my favorite thus far.Unlike Two Point Hospital, decorations actually matter! What I Did Not Like It's clunky and buggy.  Guests get stuck all the time.  Reloading a save can cause certain items to be inaccessible.  Can't paint where walls meet, so they are always stuck the same color.There is a ton to unlock, which is good and bad.  I don't have the patience to find an exhibit, get it to pristine, and then to unlock all of the upgrades on it.  Not to mention a bunch of decor and other items locked behind analyzing exhibits.  Plus, to obtain some of the best ratings (or "buzz"), certain exhibits have to be placed near others or certain decorations.  It can limit freedom a bit.  Lastly, as exhibits are found, they need to be placed.  I'm someone who likes to have everything set up nicely and neatly.  Can't really do that here without a lot of effort to tear things down, then re-build.  I did that with one map, and I am still not happy with it, and it's hard to motivate myself to do it again.There is a lot of waiting around.  Waiting to get new exhibits, waiting for employees to heal, waiting to get exhibits analyzed.  It's a very creative game, and maybe a lot of time is meant to be spent in that, but I'm not that creative.While it makes sense, I couldn't stay in one map.  I had to go to new maps to unlock things there, then go back to previous maps to expand those, and so on.  I wanted to stay in the supernatural map more, and basically couldn't until I did maps I didn't want to do. Why I Stopped Playing I think it's the best Two Point game.  Hospital was way too easy and nothing mattered.  University just wasn't great overall.  So Museum is a nice change of pace, but still plagued by problems the previous games had.  I had my fun and may come back to it later. Disclaimer I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things.  Keep that in mind when reading my reviews.  If I do not have a complaint, then the game must be special!

Place exhibits, tend to them, find new exhibits, cater to guests, all that.  It works decently well.While I didn't get too far, my favorite type of museum is the supernatural.  The look, the exhibits, everything about it is my favorite thus far.Unlike Two Point Hospital, decorations actually matter! What I Did Not Like It's clunky and buggy.  Guests get stuck all the time.  Reloading a save can cause certain items to be inaccessible.  Can't paint where walls meet, so they are always stuck the same color.There is a ton to unlock, which is good and bad.  I don't have the patience to find an exhibit, get it to pristine, and then to unlock all of the upgrades on it.  Not to mention a bunch of decor and other items locked behind analyzing exhibits.  Plus, to obtain some of the best ratings (or "buzz"), certain exhibits have to be placed near others or certain decorations.  It can limit freedom a bit.  Lastly, as exhibits are found, they need to be placed.  I'm someone who likes to have everything set up nicely and neatly.  Can't really do that here without a lot of effort to tear things down, then re-build.  I did that with one map, and I am still not happy with it, and it's hard to motivate myself to do it again.There is a lot of waiting around.  Waiting to get new exhibits, waiting for employees to heal, waiting to get exhibits analyzed.  It's a very creative game, and maybe a lot of time is meant to be spent in that, but I'm not that creative.While it makes sense, I couldn't stay in one map.  I had to go to new maps to unlock things there, then go back to previous maps to expand those, and so on.  I wanted to stay in the supernatural map more, and basically couldn't until I did maps I didn't want to do. Why I Stopped Playing I think it's the best Two Point game. content: \n								Do you like Tycoon games? You'll probably like this one! It's silly in the same way that Two Point Hospital and Two Point Campus are, and it's fun to engage in the build/decorate cycles. content: \n								I have played this game for almost an entire day at this point. I really can say that I love this game and it has made me look further into the company at their other games (Which are awesome too). There are so many good things about this game including the main mechanic which is building. I love the themes, search bar to quickly navigate, and how you can go into grid mode and a free place mode. There are genuinely very few negatives I have about this game which is super surprising considering how new the game is. The first thing I would LOVE is to have a more customizable option for the criminal activity. It gets to the point where playing just isn't fun because I have three separate buildings and am aiming for 5 stars but despite having 10-20+ cops there is just too much criminal activity to combat. Second, I would love to see more narrowed down objectives for the curator levels. Once you're at a certain level the goals are, "Get 4 stars across every museum," which just becomes not very fun because I am museum hopping and it doesn't feel super attainable, but more grindey... Other than those two points I feel like this game has HUGE potential and I will absolutely be playing it more and exploring sandbox after I finish the campaign mode. Super well done here, really cannot recommend it more if you like games like zoo-builders, building games, sims, etc. :)

content: \n								As a lover of their two previous games, I am thoroughly enjoying Two Point Museum. It feels a bit more "scripted" than the previous two games, but I think the game benefits from this linearity. Building Hospitals and Schools became a sprawling endeavor that made construction a macro perspective, I ended up using blueprints a lot and made plug and play efficiency machines. Two Point Museum lends itself to more organic floor layouts that I found myself tinkering with more overtime than previous games. No two problems have the same solution and the buildings are a great constraint. It feels a lot more like an evolving puzzle than the ant farm of Hospital and University where you set up the rooms and waited for benchmarks to be met. Decorations have never been easier to use and the new partition wall and staff door system is a great addition that i wish could be added to the older games. My only complaint so far is the rabbit-hole quest system. I really enjoyed the archeology classes in TP University and was sad when I realized the mechanics wouldn't be making a return with this game. I understand the scope creep of including locations and mechanics for each of the zones, but the static, flat maps where the quests are chosen are rather underwhelming and clunky to use. I'm already missing the 3D world map from TP Hospital. Overall a great game I will be playing to completion but I'm unsure how much replay value I will get from this game's mechanics compared to the previous two games.

content: \n								I don’t often leave reviews but I feel this game beyond deserves one! This game knocks its predecessors out of the water, it’s funny, beautifully executed and the type of game you can get lost in! content: \n								If you already enjoy Two Point games (either TP Hospital or TP Campus), this is the best iteration on the theme of the lot. Ridiculously silly, tons of content you're constantly discovering, and hella engrossing. It's well worth your time and money.If you've never played a Two Point game before: It's a management/tycoon sim, where you run a series of Museums of different themes. The game starts you out easy, with only a few factors to consider, and slowly and accessibly ramps up the complexity as you progress. You have to manage your staff as well as your guest's needs, and look after the exhibits you've collected, all while building, designing, and decorating your museum. To collect more exhibits, you have to go on expeditions: rabbit holes you send your staff out to, where they look for new things to display in your museum. A bunch of fun random events can happen on these expeditions, and the thing you're looking for isn't always guaranteed, but they're always worth it. The more expeditions you embark on, the more exhibits, perks, EXP, and other bonuses you'll acquire, and you'll unlock more places to explore and more fun things to find and collect.The main thing about Two Point games is the humour; very wry, very silly, very self-effacing, very British. The music soundtrack is actually a radio station, with various silly segments voiced by various DJs and announcers, adding a lot to giggle along to as you play. The exhibits themselves are likewise silly; fossils of "ancient" floppy disks, the bones of a "nibblesaurus", a man-eating plant that can turn people into clowns, and so much more; and your guests will interact with these exhibits in a bunch of very silly, very entertaining ways. I spend so much time just watching them, it's a bunch of fun.There's tons of space to build your museums, and lots of themes with lots of different story beats and challenges that make each play session interesting. There's also a sandbox mode, but even after 80 hours of playing I have yet to exhaust the content of the challenges and haven't tried it yet. If all this sounds at all like fun to you, then give it a try! I've put so many hours into it, and I don't feel my attention waning yet.Gotta get pristine quality exhibits of everythiiiiing!! D:

content: \n								This is the first Two Point game I really loved, but the technical issues hold it back. It's a lot more fun collecting and arranging things for your museum than the other themes in the series so far, and it's addicting to push your expeditions further to see what other things there are to collect. However the game is fairly buggy and the further you get into the game the laggier and buggier it gets. I've had a few soft locks and bugs that persisted through restarting my game. I also have a 4090 and beefed up computer but at some point you'll get his with CPU lag. Certain buttons and tool were taking seconds to load that used to be instant and I got tired of it. Pros:-The collect and show aspect is addicting-The management feeds into the loop wellCons:-Many Bugs-Your museum will hit a CPU wall if it gets too big that will really hamper playing.

content: \n								This is close to being the perfect game. After 300 hours, I only have positive thoughts. Technically, there are no issues - no crashing, no glitches, no game breaking bugs; which is almost unheard of in a brand new game. As for the game play, it's engaging and just plain fun. Each museum has its own well developed storyline that still allows you the freedom to build as you see fit. The only downside I've experienced so far is with the theft system. I would get frustrated when thieves would make off with an exhibit that took time to build and was necessary for progression, but I learned how to work with the system. You can't just sit back and watch what happens, you have to be proactive. There are security doors, guards, cameras and chairs and when you get the notice that a thief has been spotted, you just pause the game, grab a guard and drop him on the thief's head for instant capture. It's not 100%, but it's much better than watching thieves make off with your hard work cause the camera room guard was on break and the other guards were gathering donations on the other side of the building. Zones also help. I don't know who came up with the idea of zones, but I love it. Zones allow you to designate staff to a certain part of the building, not just a certain job! Overall, this ticks all the boxes for a fantastic sim, and I can't wait for the first expansion.

content: \n								This game has everything, from managing, exploring, building, to Easter eggs. At the moment I'm writing this, I have 80 hours of playtime, and I still haven't finished the campaign. I'm not even close, as the difficulty increases with each star.Pros: A great variety of building options and things you can construct in the museum. The maps are interconnected, so what you build in one museum can be built in another. The game guides you through the campaign to the next maps, and you continuously return to them (unlike in Two Point Hospital, where you’re done with a map once you finish it; here, you return after a few rounds). Graphics are great. The campaign is longer than some AAA titles, and that doesn't even include the Sandbox mode. Adjustable difficulty settings—building, destroying buildings for money or not, allowing or disallowing the movement of exhibits. Twitch integration (like Cult of the Lamb), which allows your followers to participate in the game.Cons: !!!!! There’s no option to select multiple items at once, which is a huge problem because each exhibit has so many decorations, etc. As soon as you want to move an exhibit even slightly, you have to manually move 15-20 other items as well, and then move or sell and buy them again and place them back. If you have a weaker PC or, like me, a 4K monitor, after building more structures and adding many attractions (especially aquariums), the game starts to lag. Lowering the graphics didn’t help, and nothing I tried worked—you're stuck with your PC's capabilities because each fish in every aquarium is rendered individually. The helicopter often bugs out for me. I say "often," but it’s just annoying, and the game needs to be restarted when this happens. The requirements for stars are just tedious—you wait for hours to bring in new exhibits just to get one star, and then you need even more.Overall, if you didn’t catch it through the 80 hours, I highly recommend this game. It’s a simulation game that currently has no equal in what it offers in the market (and I’ve tried plenty), and the developers are constantly adding more features and fixing issues. The DLC for this will just add a lot more gameplay.

The different museum themes all bring different gameplay mechanics to the fore and they do some fun fantastical ideas with them, i.e. prehistory is the standard museum stuff, but supernatural has you have hotel rooms for ghosts where you have to fulfill their needs, marine life is essentially a simpler Megaquarium, Space exhibits have anomalies which activate if placed near smaller cosmic relics and other anomalies which grant benefits, etc. Game’s got a lot of goofy charm too, like how the plant exhibits can just turn guest into ♥♥♥♥ like vampires and clowns. There are some hiccups here and there, like I’ve run into some bugs where guests just get stuck or an exhibit kept giving me an invalid placement prompt until I reloaded a save, but it’s not bad. Though I do wish there was a more manual save option, because it seems just runs on auto-saves. Two Point Museum has quickly become one of my favorite tycoon games, definitely check it out.

content: \n								This game has all the right intentions, but poorly executed. It's fun, but it could have been so much more with little effort, and that honestly bothers me. The creative options are extremely limited. Sandbox mode for example, isn't a sandbox mode at all. You can't create from scratch, you will always be stuck with a pre-set building. Secondly, even in sandbox mode, all items will still need to be unlocked by achievements. As for career mode, it's fun for a little while, but it gets monotone fast. Mainly because your museum has limited space and limited means to personalize it. The choices to make it more simply aren't there. For example, to decorate, you get the choice out of 1 potted plant, 2 types of couches (1 big, 1 small), 1 type of snack table, no salon tables or eating tables, no kitchens for staff, 1 type of toilet/bathroom area choice etc etc. Every items offers 1 or 2 of each, which means your museum looks the same every single time. You can't create a certain aesthetic this way. Even more aggravating is the fact that the exhibitions found by your searchteam will be completely random. So they can come back from an excursion with 5x the same item back-to-back, while not coming back with an item that you are still missing. I think this was meant to create a more 'challenging' collection, but honestly, it's just repetitive and frustrating. I also would have liked to see more managerial options in this game. F.e. there's not enough ways to encourage or stimulate your employees. If they get sad, well... all you can do is up their paycheck. You can't choose their break-hours, or a bonus, or give them an item. You can choose which task they perform, but that's about all. Same with your finances, it's over simplified to the point where I've always found myself with a ton of money, but what can I do with it? I can't buy more materials or items, because that has to be bought with 'Kudos' credits, a separate system that basically makes money feel very obsolete. My biggest pet-peeve however was lighting. The game is seriously off on this. If you don't know how to do lighting right in a game, then simply don't mess around with dark/light/shadows etc. You have rooms that are bright, and rooms that are very dark for no reason whatsoever. If you research this issue on the internet it mostly seems to be some type of bug, but I'm not sure of anything is being done about it. F.e. My entryway will be lit up, but the gift shop in the entryway will be super dark. Both rooms have windows but those don't help at all. I'm left to wonder what the point of windows even is. Lamps are also non-existent in the game, so no help there.Conclusion: Well intended game, but it just should have been so, so much more. Especially for 30 Euro's.

Secondly, even in sandbox mode, all items will still need to be unlocked by achievements. As for career mode, it's fun for a little while, but it gets monotone fast. Mainly because your museum has limited space and limited means to personalize it. The choices to make it more simply aren't there. For example, to decorate, you get the choice out of 1 potted plant, 2 types of couches (1 big, 1 small), 1 type of snack table, no salon tables or eating tables, no kitchens for staff, 1 type of toilet/bathroom area choice etc etc. Every items offers 1 or 2 of each, which means your museum looks the same every single time. You can't create a certain aesthetic this way. Even more aggravating is the fact that the exhibitions found by your searchteam will be completely random. So they can come back from an excursion with 5x the same item back-to-back, while not coming back with an item that you are still missing. I think this was meant to create a more 'challenging' collection, but honestly, it's just repetitive and frustrating. I also would have liked to see more managerial options in this game. F.e. there's not enough ways to encourage or stimulate your employees. If they get sad, well... all you can do is up their paycheck. You can't choose their break-hours, or a bonus, or give them an item. You can choose which task they perform, but that's about all. Same with your finances, it's over simplified to the point where I've always found myself with a ton of money, but what can I do with it? I can't buy more materials or items, because that has to be bought with 'Kudos' credits, a separate system that basically makes money feel very obsolete. My biggest pet-peeve however was lighting. The game is seriously off on this. If you don't know how to do lighting right in a game, then simply don't mess around with dark/light/shadows etc. You have rooms that are bright, and rooms that are very dark for no reason whatsoever. If you research this issue on the internet it mostly seems to be some type of bug, but I'm not sure of anything is being done about it. F.e. My entryway will be lit up, but the gift shop in the entryway will be super dark. Both rooms have windows but those don't help at all. I'm left to wonder what the point of windows even is. Lamps are also non-existent in the game, so no help there.Conclusion: Well intended game, but it just should have been so, so much more. Especially for 30 Euro's.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.
