content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I really like this game, so why a no?Well, it's the little things, and there's many of them.Let's start with the positive:- Funny- Building your own museum is a very enjoyable experience, some theme's I enjoy more than others but that's OK.Let's move on to the negative- Staff getting stuck, and then resigning. Yep, this is the most frustrating one for me. It probably also has a bit to do with my design choices, I kinda like cramped, using space optimally. And staff get's stuck doing things. Sometimes this means they can't get to tha choppa either, and you can't cancel the expedition. So you end up with a stuck chopper. Reload fortunately helps most of the times, and still this is a very annoying bug- Pathing is atrocious. I sometimes set up a new tour, only to get it to path completely wrong and make it way longer than it needs to be, or it bugs out making exhibits unreachable by visitors.- Can be incredibly grindy, and not in a good way. To get all the pristine exhibits, there's a leveling system for each POI that determines the quality of an exhibit. Now getting them does not seem to be random, but instead seems to be rotational. This also means that if a POI has 4 exhibits, and you only need 1 more pristine, you'll need to do 4 runs to get a chance for pristine. And sometimes, even at max level, even doing a detailed expedition to increase quality -  oddly enough, you'll still be getting a lot of lower quality exhibits. Now, granted, this is probably a lot less frustrating than having it be random and being very unlucky, it's still frustrating and poorly designed. (Someway of upgrading multiple epics into a pristine, would be neat).- This brings me to cursed objects and phantom for the supernatural theme...The objects can get a RANDOM effect that's either negative or positive. You could counter this by installing an extremely rare perk.... But it honestly is just quicker and smarter to find one with a positive effect, instead of grinding for the perk.... also, one with a positive effect doesn't waste a perk slot this way.... Either way, this adds a random roll to rotational loot, meaning for some pristine cursed objects I had to do over 30 expeditions.... which is literally just waiting so you can continue building your museum.... it's frustrating beyond words.Phantoms are a bit less frustrating, but these also have a random subclass. Which means if you'd want another one, you can keep grinding for another pristine and hope it rolls what you'd like. (Like a specific knight for a specific famous ghost)- The UI is pretty trash. Notifications hiding buttons, or the staff list not sorting correctly. Missing trait information when you want to train your dudes, so you need to go back into another menu to find out if you're training the right person in the right job..... it's ludicrous that it got into the game in this way. Not to mention that staff sorting on type doesn't seem to work, so when you get up to 50 experts, and you need to find a certain one for a certain theme, you'll end up scrolling through all of your staff to find them - why can't we sort or exclude so we can only focus on experts for a certain theme?- The traits are nonsensical. Most of them are just silly. 25% faster training? You only get to do that 5 times on a staff member, then it's useless. Nimble and Loyal are by far the best perks - movement speed and pay reduction? yes please. The rest.... eh. Globetrotter and Photographic memory aren't as great as they seem. In later areas you'll be relying on skills of your non-expedition staff, because your expedition staff has a different skillset..... Analytical is another I get (1 per theme) for faster analyses, but I honestly think I can even forgo that, because as with expeditions, at some point you don't need to analyze anything anymore + it seems that anyone can do it anyway, so why not train it for something else that it's doing more of the time? Eloquent being my top pick for tour guides, with nimble even better.... and when you have all theme's unlocked, getting experts for a certain theme is quite tedious, paying 2500 for 1 pick 9 days later (and it disappears too if you don't check the hiring menu fast enough, I lost quite a few prospects this way just getting caught up in museum design)- Big lack of controls - for instance, there's no way (like frostpunk 1+2 do) to browse through a certain type of item. So for instance, let's say I want to upgrade all my filters for my aquariums because I got the upgrade, so why not, right? I have to find them, click them one by one, and upgrade them, one by one, instead of being able to press a button like ] to select the next one of that type.It's the same for speakers, and anything else really - for instance, I was setting up ambiance in the maritime part of my museum, I set up a speaker, which means selecting the appropriate ambiance theme, then copied it, thinking it would also copy the ambiance setting - it doesn't. So I had to go through all my speakers, and manually set them to the right ambiance. So tedious. Same with tour stations.- Auto Assign assigns at random it seems, which brings me back to horrible UI. I'm scrolling through so many staff to find the ones that have skills that counter events.... I don't understand why the staff that have the skills to counter these events don't show up on top...?? I really don't. Or, that if you press auto assign, it actually picks the ones that counter events, or, a button that assigns the last assigned crew to the POI?I think these are the big ones for me, that make this game a nuisance at times. I have a love hate relationship with this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating. And to top that off, some of the bugs, like pathing and staff getting stuck, are known for over a month, and not been fixed. Sadly.So I'm going to put this on no for now, and continue building my museum, because that part *is* fun. Just... the state of the game, in my opinion, is a bit subpar.

content: \n								I can't play this game anymore. After 102 hours played, I've had too many problems with it erasing my progress. Sure, I'm on a laptop, which is a lot less reliable than a desktop PC, but I have never had this issue with the previous two-point games. I can only assume its the over-arching campaign messing with everything. Which is a fun concept, but frustrating at times. The first time I had a problem, my entire campaign was gone, whole game, disappeared. Thankfully I tried to play the game on my steam deck once, so I was able to obtain most of my campaign from that (only losing a week of progress). Then today, another loss. This time, I still have my entire campaign, and all my stars thankfully, but the level I was playing reset to the beginning! It still says I have 3 stars on the level, but the story is actually reset and my museum, that I had to design twice already, is erased. SO, basically when I want to restart a level by choice, I can't, there is no option to do so (unlike in the other games), all you can do is bulldoze the level. Yet my progress can apparently be erased at anytime on a whim, without a choice, and that's okay? And there is no fixing it or preventing it. And for the icing on the cake, I tried to back up my game from steam, backing it up each night, trying to prevent losing my campaign again. So when I attempted to restore my game using one of the steam backups, it doesn't work at all! It didn't restore the level I was playing so what's the point? The steam backup uses different files from what I can see. So based on my forewarning, maybe you can try to copy the save files from the two point museum folders on your pc, instead of going through steam?? I'm not sure. Either way, good luck!Personally, I can't play this game anymore. At this rate, I'd never progress in the game. If I have to redo that same level again, I'll go crazy. I can't take any more destroyed progress. I'll wait a while, a long while, until the game has had a lot more bug fixes and updates. I need a lot of time away from it, but I can't imagine it will have the same issues in a year or two. Until then, I repeat myself, I can't play this game.

content: \n								Disappointing.  If you like decorating, you will probably like this game.  If you like the more strategy/tactics gameplay of TPH, you may not like this game.  For me, once the initial excitement of a new Two Point game wore off, I struggled to stay interested in playing.  For a while I had to force myself to play, until I just stopped. I loved TPH (still do)One nice aspect of the game is the ability to create and edit your own buildings rather than being stuck with awkwardly designed buildings.  It gives you a lot of freedom for building and decorating. I wish these changes could be added to the previous Two Point games.  Unfortunately, outside of those mechanics, the gameplay in TPM is lacking.  The staff window displays little information, so you have to constantly bounce between different windows to find out information about your staff.   TPH was so much better in this regard.   I'm not sure who thought that providing less information, for something you need to look at constantly,  was a good idea.There are multiple museum types (though you can display all types of exhibits in the same museum, once unlocked), which I looked forward to unlocking.  Unfortunately, other than the cosmetics, the museum exhibits are essentially the same.  Other than the Marine Life museum where you build aquariums and fill them with fish, everything is just about placing static objects, so each museum feels very much like the previous ones, but with a different coat of paint.  The science museum, no science stuff going on, just objects to place.  Space museum, no space stuff, just alien objects to place. Probably the coolest is the supernatural museum objects, but still, you are mostly just placing objects.There are fewer rooms to build.  Outside of aquariums for the fish, exhibits are not room dependent.  Though, you can build your own walls to create rooms to segregate exhibits of the same type.  While this gives freedom of design, you can't copy or move the rooms, which is a pain when you want to redesign, or expand your museum.  Again, for people that like decorating, this likely won't be an issue, it's just not for me.

content: \n								My Two Point universum currently consists of Hospital and Museum - the first one is a chaotic management sim with some interior decorating on the side, while the second one is interior/exterior decoration sim with grindy lottery machine in the background. That saying - building and decorating is fun. There are plenty of decorations to choose from, and you can make almost anything with the variety of exhibits available in the game. There are small and gigantic ones, all of them are funny (my personal favorite is Lava Lamp), and they fit the theme. Botany is a little finicky as it's a bit all over the place with sizes and looks (why there is a sandy base but no sandy floors?!), but players have already done amazing setups with them. The game looks really pretty, but there are major drops in fps with 200+ guests (there are workarounds, but be prepared to play in <30 fps at some point if you aim for a museum of everything). Workers' and visitors' logic works most of the time - occasional bugs happen, making guests stuck, but it's not affecting the museum score almost at all. Your staff on the other hand... Micromanaging from time to time was necessary. I don't mind that - for me it's part of the fun, but others may disagree.I couldn't escape from comparing Two Point titles as I was constantly missing something in Museum gameplay... At first, I had so much fun collecting dinosaur bones, placing fossils and space anomalies, but from now and then I was interrupted by waiting. It didn't feel bad at first - just slow down a little till the next helicopter comes back or until I sell some Gubbins Plushies to make the budget. The further I got on each map, the longer those waiting periods became, and at some point, it was just annoying. Expeditions get grindy as hell at some point - lasting 60+ days with requirements that not always allow to use staff with Pilot trait (quicker expeditions) or with requirements so specific that either I need to sacrifice staff member or recruit and train someone just for this one Point of Interest (that takes SO MUCH TIME)... Worst part is - sometimes you need to go on them multiple times to get everything! If there are multi-part exhibits, then you're on the mercy of RNGesus... Same goes for hunting Pristine condition exhibits or more of them for knowledge analysis... It's ridiculous how much time I wasted just grinding and waiting instead of having fun by creating themed rooms and displays... It's such a shame that nobody stopped and asked developers - is making expeditions harder any fun for the target audience? It's not... In my opinion, this game should be about creativity and the joy of building, even if that makes it shorter. Satisfaction from playing does not include time perceived as wasted.I still think this game can bring a lot of fun for people who would like to curate a funny exhibit collection in almost stress free game. Developers did a good job that for me was worth the full price (and support which comes with it). Is this game cozy? Yes. Will it annoy you to hell and back while not being as hectic as Hospital? Also yes.

content: \n								My Two Point universum currently consists of Hospital and Museum - the first one is a chaotic management sim with some interior decorating on the side, while the second one is interior/exterior decoration sim with grindy lottery machine in the background. That saying - building and decorating is fun. There are plenty of decorations to choose from, and you can make almost anything with the variety of exhibits available in the game. There are small and gigantic ones, all of them are funny (my personal favorite is Lava Lamp), and they fit the theme. Botany is a little finicky as it's a bit all over the place with sizes and looks (why there is a sandy base but no sandy floors?!), but players have already done amazing setups with them. The game looks really pretty, but there are major drops in fps with 200+ guests (there are workarounds, but be prepared to play in <30 fps at some point if you aim for a museum of everything). Workers' and visitors' logic works most of the time - occasional bugs happen, making guests stuck, but it's not affecting the museum score almost at all. Your staff on the other hand... Micromanaging from time to time was necessary. I don't mind that - for me it's part of the fun, but others may disagree.I couldn't escape from comparing Two Point titles as I was constantly missing something in Museum gameplay... At first, I had so much fun collecting dinosaur bones, placing fossils and space anomalies, but from now and then I was interrupted by waiting. It didn't feel bad at first - just slow down a little till the next helicopter comes back or until I sell some Gubbins Plushies to make the budget. The further I got on each map, the longer those waiting periods became, and at some point, it was just annoying. Expeditions get grindy as hell at some point - lasting 60+ days with requirements that not always allow to use staff with Pilot trait (quicker expeditions) or with requirements so specific that either I need to sacrifice staff member or recruit and train someone just for this one Point of Interest (that takes SO MUCH TIME)... Worst part is - sometimes you need to go on them multiple times to get everything! If there are multi-part exhibits, then you're on the mercy of RNGesus... Same goes for hunting Pristine condition exhibits or more of them for knowledge analysis... It's ridiculous how much time I wasted just grinding and waiting instead of having fun by creating themed rooms and displays... It's such a shame that nobody stopped and asked developers - is making expeditions harder any fun for the target audience? It's not... In my opinion, this game should be about creativity and the joy of building, even if that makes it shorter. Satisfaction from playing does not include time perceived as wasted.I still think this game can bring a lot of fun for people who would like to curate a funny exhibit collection in almost stress free game. Developers did a good job that for me was worth the full price (and support which comes with it). Is this game cozy? Yes. Will it annoy you to hell and back while not being as hectic as Hospital? Also yes.

content: \n								Two Point Museum is a really fun and creative addition to the Two Point series. The core gameplay loop is super engaging – building and managing your own museum filled with all kinds of quirky exhibits is both satisfying and often hilarious. The game's signature charm and humor are definitely here, and they make the experience feel light-hearted and enjoyable.One of the features I absolutely love is the souvenir shop. It adds a lot of personality and fits perfectly in a museum setting. However, I was a bit disappointed by the limited decoration options for it. I’d love to have more ways to make the shop unique or themed to match the exhibits nearby.The cafeteria is another great idea in theory, but in practice, it feels a bit underwhelming. Visitors rarely use it, which makes it feel like wasted space. It would be nice if its usefulness could be balanced a bit better in future updates.Despite these small issues, the rest of the game is really well-designed, with a lot of attention to detail and some very clever ideas. Each level feels fresh and encourages you to think creatively about how to layout and organize your museum. If you're a fan of management sims or loved Two Point Hospital/Campus, this game is absolutely worth playing!

content: \n								Out of the last two games in the series, Two Point Museum is most similar (thankfully) to Two Point Hospital, in that your guests queue at the start of your building, then you focus on designing the most efficient pathway for them through the facility while keeping their needs high.Two Point Museum adds a lot of cool stuff to the formula to where I can confidently say it's the best game in the series so far. For example: To get new exhibits for your museum you have to send your staff on expeditions Indiana Jones style. They bring you back loot boxes to open, so lots of dopamine. Expeditions can be made a lot easier if your staff have good skills so training is important and you get attached to your best people. There's a LOT of exhibits of all different types which helps the game stay fresh for a long time. They all work in different ways, like having to collect lots of dinosaur bones to assemble the whole skeleton, ghost that demand their own room, or aquariums where fish can be bred. It's not a super hard game but you definitely need to have a better grasp on your cash flow than the previous games. Expeditions, salaries, training and building are all expensive so you need to focus on maximising your income to keep growing at a good pace.  You can now paint walls and floors with different colours and textures, and place fake walls wherever you want. I spent so long designing and redesigning my museums, creating themed rooms and figuring out how to insert cute little rest stops or coffee spots without breaking my museum theme.There are a few annoyances that I hope they iron out: Staff level SO slowly. I've played for nearly 80 hours and never once got a staff member to max level. If you don't have a certain skill you need for an expedition it can take an eternity to level someone up high enough to train them. Staff can also die in some cases on missions and losing a high-level person is devastating. Most of my playtime I adored the expedition/loot box mechanic, however after playing for like 50 hours it did get a bit tedious. Sometimes you don't have much to change about your museum and you're just running the same expedition over and over and over with the game on max speed. I wish there was at least a way to automatically re-do the same expedition repeatedly so I didn't have to click so much. Thieves will appear quite often to try to steal exhibits from you. Even when I fill my museum with guards and station them at various choke points, they would still get away sometimes. I would watch a thief sprint past a guard who does a slow surprise animation then starts chasing once they are already way ahead. And several other guards in the path of the thief will ignore him because the game says a guard is already assigned to chasing him.

content: \n								Two Point games have been going from strength to strength, and this isn't the one that is going to break that tradition.It's a bit of a departure from Hospital and Campus in that it's a bit more involved, and that's a good thing but it can take some getting used to.The game play is pretty much the same as the previous games, build something, make it pretty and have it used and enjoyed by staff and visitors alike.The usual humour of it all is here, the graphics are well presented as always and there are some fun little animations to keep a look out for.The game play is, sort of the same - But different - The Museums are all connected to each other this time with each one giving you a specialisation or a theme to start with, but once you've learnt how that works you can incorporate that into your other Museums. I guess it's kind of more "Open World" this time around if you can have such a thing in these games.You can no longer reset a level if you make a mistake and things start to go wrong, which is the part you're going to have to get used to - Or, I have at least - No - This time around you've got to fix the problems and not just write them off as a bad go.Which also means you need to pay attention to the Tutorials as you only seem to be able to get them once and so if you get a bit click happy you might miss something you later need to know - WHICH - Is exactly what I did when I got the second Museum and ended up with me restarting the whole thing, which is how I also know you can't restart Museums...I'll admit I was a bit put off with this approach at first, but once I knew about it I could work with it and not just think I knew everything the game was trying to teach me because I'd played the earlier games.And, since - It actually makes the whole thing more enjoyable to go from one Museum to another to complete the tasks you need to progress the other(s) further - Bringing more knowledge to an earlier level etc.There also seems to be more of a point to micro managing things in this game as well, there have been a couple of things I've ignored in previous games unless I had to pay attention to them and in this game you can't, or not as much anyways.So - Yeah - Loving that they've not just made a carbon copy of the last game and slapped some new paint on it, which I'd probably have enjoyed as well. But this is something different to get my head around and I'm still loving it just as much.

content: \n								This new game from Two Point is filled with the usual humor, which made it enjoyable for about two-thirds of the 83 hours I played the game.  Then the grind got overwhelming. content: \n								I cannot recommend Two Point Museum enough! Not only does it fulfil the Curator fantasy but does it in a way that keeps the game play light, fun, engaging and satisfying. So many surprises in exhibits and guest interactions with them, as well as fun gags, puns, and a generally funny tone. The Two Point team have filled the 6 different streams of science with amusing wish-list artefacts that have quite often delighted me, as well as items that are unlock-able, craft-able and up-gradable.Each different stream has it's own quirks and features that make each one worthwhile. I think there might be something interesting for everyone and players will undoubtedly have their favourite streams. I'm partial to the paranormal, prehistory, space and science, but also enjoy botany and marine life - the sunken civilisation artefacts are great!Developing several distinct museums at the same time across the map has been a fantastic idea as you stop and start each one as developments in one affect change for the others. The interest in all subjects is motivated to try and uncover all artefacts for each stream and if you tire of one museum you can pop over to another and back again as the need takes you. Your advancements go with you so you can unlock locations on your expedition map that are useful for a different museum and although this isn't extensive it is enough to get you jumping back to a different museum to try to uncover what the new artefact might be.The system of returning to a location to get a better version of the exhibits is good, but I would say it should be easier to get pristine versions with higher experienced experts otherwise less patient players may give up too soon.The game has a few little bugs and hiccups here and there but nothing that is game breaking and the team appears to be on top of them. There might need to be extra ways to buy or trade artefacts and resources from the inventories of other museums as they can be rare or hard to get and needed at another of your museum locations. Instead of just buying or trading the other museum has to go through the same long hit-and-miss process of trying to get an artefact, which feels like too much grinding.I am looking forward to more museum themes in the future - whatever they are - but I'm hoping for artworks, geology and cryptids. I would also welcome some additional artefacts for the current themes.Overall I recommend the game to anyone with a sense of humour, with a like of management sims and an interest in sciences. An instant classic for me! Great work Two Point!

content: \n								As every Two Point Game this game is really fun to play. Good jokes, nice optics, funny interactions. It is a Two Point Game, so i spare the review about the game mechanics shared with TP Hospital and TP Campus. It feels the same, in a good way. Some other mechanics felt really good at first, but became annoying later. There are Expeditions in the game, which is how one unlocks new stuff. After an expidition, you basically gain a lootbox, with a (new) item in it. This is allways exciting when you start new expeditions to new areas and you don't know what to find. But once you found something, and you want the objects of desire in good quality (which is important for many reasons), you have to rerun the expedition over and over, and over, and over, and over, and over, and o.. you get the idea. If you are lucky, you only have to do the same expedition 10-12 times. If you are unlucky, like me, you repeat some expeditions 50 times or more. That's like chewing old gum. There is no function in the game (at least after 63h in) to automate this process or to tell the team you send what to look for. There is one item (common found) i still havent found in perfect quality, however everything else from the same expedition (extremely rare finds) i got plenty of perfect quality ones. This function is so extremely repetetive, that i stoped playing the game for now. I could also just dont care for perfect quality and continue progress.. but thats just not what i wanna do, and the game intends you to find the good quality stuff. Hopefully they do some quality of life changes to exhibitions. Otherwise i have to let the game rest aside until i finally feel motivated enough to start opening lootboxes again. Besides that i'd recommend the game, as its fun overall.

content: \n								A masterpiece of museum madness!Two Point Museum is an absolute gem – a whimsical, pun-fueled joyride that had me giggling from the first exhibition to all kind of things - even if it's just the silly animations people do with the exibits! If you’re a fan of tongue-in-cheek humor, clever wordplay, and wildly imaginative scenarios, then this is the game for you. I couldn’t stop laughing at the absurd yet strangely plausible exhibitions (I mean, who doesn’t want to see an ancient artifact misidentified as a fancy coffee machine?) – and don’t even get me started on the staff descriptions. Hilariously useless? Brilliantly eccentric? Yes, please!The puns? Chef’s kiss. I found myself reading every pop-up and notification just to catch another sneaky joke or silly twist on museum jargon. It’s the kind of game that rewards you for paying attention, and I love that. It’s like living in a Monty Python sketch… but with more fossils and fewer dead parrots.That said, while I’m having a blast running my chaotic kingdom of curators and curious visitors, there is some room for polish in the menus and staff management systems. Juggling multiple scenarios and keeping track of my increasingly wacky employees can feel like herding caffeinated cats through an art gallery – amusing, but sometimes a bit much. The UI could use a bit of streamlining, and better tools for sorting staff or prioritizing tasks would go a long way.But honestly? I’m excited. You can tell the devs are having fun with this, and I have high hopes for future updates. With a little tuning and some quality-of-life improvements, Two Point Museum could become a modern classic in the sim genre. For now, I’m fully on board for the ride – puns, prehistoric plants, and all.Two Point team – please keep the silliness coming!

Looking forward to any DLC areas they might be coming up with!

content: \n								I am a big fan of the Two Point series of games. They strike the perfect balance for me of having a lot of freedom of expression, without being too bogged down in a lot of extra (I can't get into the Planet games for this reason, despite them being great games in their own right). I like a game where I have a solid goal through-line; scenarios that give me something to aim for, rather than a big sandbox and being left to my own devices - granted this game does have that as well, but I am always much more focused on the more structured stuff.Said structure is a lot different to the previous two game's format. You don't go from one scenario to the next now. Instead you have 5 museums that you will bounce between, each one with their own story lines, and each one helping the other by expanding what is available in the others. It's a very different change of pace, and it puts a lot of emphasis on each areas different feel and goals. I'm unsure if I prefer this style to the more traditional levels, but I had a lot of fun with it all, so I guess I can't say I disliked it. This is another good game in the series. And the name of the game for this particular outing, is customisation. You have a lot more tools than you've had in previous games, to make your museums look nice and more dynamic than just a series of box shaped rooms. Which makes sense, since there is a lot of emphasis on this mechanic. If you want to do well, you need to make the museums look good; coherent themes among exhibits, matching themes and the like. And I think the game does a grand job in showing you what is possible through the starting zone in the scenario mode, along with smaller challenge maps that they call Pop Up Museums. They really gave a me a lot of ideas about how I could improve my own aesthetics.You'll be travelling to prehistoric dig sites, to the bottom of the ocean and then up into space, to give you a nice variety of exhibit types to flesh out. If you liked the humour in the other games, you'll like this one as well. My only real gripe with it is that I felt like the radio announcers were repeating themselves a lot more than in previous games, perhaps because you're in the same locations for a lot longer than previously. If the aquarium museum is anything to go buy, I'd absolutely love it if they tackled zoos next. I'm sure they'd come up with all sorts of strange and interesting animals. But with Planet Zoo, I can't imagine they want to compete with it. I just feel like their design philosophies would scratch that itch the original Zoo Tycoon did all those years ago. Looking forward to any DLC areas they might be coming up with!

content: \n								This game is a TON of fun. I finished the campaign of each map zone and full knowledge/pristine every item. I did not 50 every museum because I just wanted one of each exhibit type for that map zone, you can easily hit it if you start to double up on exhibits. Seeing and designing your museum was extremely exciting and satisfying to watch happen. It is a bit different then Two Point Hospital with game play but still has that same overall fun goofy feeling, I have not played Campus yet. There are some things that would push this game to the fullest and wanted to state this here. Some of these wont become obvious if you are just playing and not trying full knowledge/pristine everything. 1. Can't replace Perks to improve your exhibit, this seems weird especially when you start doing Bungle Burrows zone. Could just replace and delete the old one, as simple as that. 2. Can’t retrain Staff, don't miss click.3. Need more keybindings, especially for Inventory so you can quickly place items down. 4. Notifications for Assistants come up too quickly when the job is empty. 5. Needs another speed up button, late game waiting around for expedition to complete can be like 5+ mins. 6. Tasks/Goals on the right side of the screen, you can minimize them but there are some that you won't care to know the progress, if you are not quick enough you can’t delete(trash can) the notification so you’ll have to just minimize, this can cause a ton of minimized notifications on the side of your screen. 7. When in mid to late game of your museum you can’t pinpoint a specific trait on employees or even get the option to train them. Example, I’d always like to run security guards with Peripheral Vision(wider view) just to help ever so little with spotting thieves. Rng can take forever to find one or sometimes you’d get two in a row. Would love a way to train traits on staff.8. Doing the same expedition over and over again, there is no “repeat same crew” or equivalent button. Every time you start it up, if you have a guy for the specific mission qualification you’d have to scroll and select them, it starts to get tedious when they are towards the bottom of the list. On top of that, the auto fill button for whatever reason does not put your employees that have the missions required qualifications it just randomises all your staff instead. That button needs to improve in a way or add another option.9. Can't go for a specific reward on expedition, no workshop project to even sink materials into for this. If you are trying to get full Knowledge/ Pristine, certain items can take FOREVER due to rng especially if there are 3+ rewards on that expedition. Later in the zones the expeditions will take many days and if you have to do the detailed(+1 quality) the speed just adds even more days. One expedition in the Bone Belt took over 100+ days and on top of that Winter/Spring time you’d have a MIA(guy will just die) if you send. 10. When in your inventory exhibits section and you hover over one of the items, it doesn’t say what the requirements are, you have to select it first, which then takes you out of your inventory. This problem comes up when you have multiple of an exhibit and you want one specific for an item, you’ll notice this in the Two Point Sea zone with how the fish need certain items while others don't want that item, so a ton of back and forth in the inventory to find the specific fish. 11. Have a setting while assigning another expedition it doesn't stop time, unless you manually pause it. This sucks when you have 2 or 3 expeditions going at once, one will be 60+ days and another can be 10 days just slows down the progress a ton. Those were the major ones that I was starting to get sour at. Again, with over 110+ hours in, I got my time and money worth out of this amazing game, I want to clarify that up to all that read this. Those above are just things you might come across that can be off putting.  Sold game, loved it, go have fun and play it!

There are some things that would push this game to the fullest and wanted to state this here. Some of these wont become obvious if you are just playing and not trying full knowledge/pristine everything. 1. Can't replace Perks to improve your exhibit, this seems weird especially when you start doing Bungle Burrows zone. Could just replace and delete the old one, as simple as that. 2. Can’t retrain Staff, don't miss click.3. Need more keybindings, especially for Inventory so you can quickly place items down. 4. Notifications for Assistants come up too quickly when the job is empty. 5. Needs another speed up button, late game waiting around for expedition to complete can be like 5+ mins. 6. Tasks/Goals on the right side of the screen, you can minimize them but there are some that you won't care to know the progress, if you are not quick enough you can’t delete(trash can) the notification so you’ll have to just minimize, this can cause a ton of minimized notifications on the side of your screen. 7. When in mid to late game of your museum you can’t pinpoint a specific trait on employees or even get the option to train them. Example, I’d always like to run security guards with Peripheral Vision(wider view) just to help ever so little with spotting thieves. If you are trying to get full Knowledge/ Pristine, certain items can take FOREVER due to rng especially if there are 3+ rewards on that expedition. Later in the zones the expeditions will take many days and if you have to do the detailed(+1 quality) the speed just adds even more days. One expedition in the Bone Belt took over 100+ days and on top of that Winter/Spring time you’d have a MIA(guy will just die) if you send. 10. When in your inventory exhibits section and you hover over one of the items, it doesn’t say what the requirements are, you have to select it first, which then takes you out of your inventory. This problem comes up when you have multiple of an exhibit and you want one specific for an item, you’ll notice this in the Two Point Sea zone with how the fish need certain items while others don't want that item, so a ton of back and forth in the inventory to find the specific fish. 11. Have a setting while assigning another expedition it doesn't stop time, unless you manually pause it. This sucks when you have 2 or 3 expeditions going at once, one will be 60+ days and another can be 10 days just slows down the progress a ton. Those above are just things you might come across that can be off putting.  Sold game, loved it, go have fun and play it!

content: \n								This game is a TON of fun. I finished the campaign of each map zone and full knowledge/pristine every item. I did not 50 every museum because I just wanted one of each exhibit type for that map zone, you can easily hit it if you start to double up on exhibits. Seeing and designing your museum was extremely exciting and satisfying to watch happen. It is a bit different then Two Point Hospital with game play but still has that same overall fun goofy feeling, I have not played Campus yet. There are some things that would push this game to the fullest and wanted to state this here. Some of these wont become obvious if you are just playing and not trying full knowledge/pristine everything. 1. Can't replace Perks to improve your exhibit, this seems weird especially when you start doing Bungle Burrows zone. Could just replace and delete the old one, as simple as that. 2. Can’t retrain Staff, don't miss click.3. Need more keybindings, especially for Inventory so you can quickly place items down. 4. Notifications for Assistants come up too quickly when the job is empty. 5. Needs another speed up button, late game waiting around for expedition to complete can be like 5+ mins. 6. Tasks/Goals on the right side of the screen, you can minimize them but there are some that you won't care to know the progress, if you are not quick enough you can’t delete(trash can) the notification so you’ll have to just minimize, this can cause a ton of minimized notifications on the side of your screen. 7. When in mid to late game of your museum you can’t pinpoint a specific trait on employees or even get the option to train them. Example, I’d always like to run security guards with Peripheral Vision(wider view) just to help ever so little with spotting thieves. Rng can take forever to find one or sometimes you’d get two in a row. Would love a way to train traits on staff.8. Doing the same expedition over and over again, there is no “repeat same crew” or equivalent button. Every time you start it up, if you have a guy for the specific mission qualification you’d have to scroll and select them, it starts to get tedious when they are towards the bottom of the list. On top of that, the auto fill button for whatever reason does not put your employees that have the missions required qualifications it just randomises all your staff instead. That button needs to improve in a way or add another option.9. Can't go for a specific reward on expedition, no workshop project to even sink materials into for this. If you are trying to get full Knowledge/ Pristine, certain items can take FOREVER due to rng especially if there are 3+ rewards on that expedition. Later in the zones the expeditions will take many days and if you have to do the detailed(+1 quality) the speed just adds even more days. One expedition in the Bone Belt took over 100+ days and on top of that Winter/Spring time you’d have a MIA(guy will just die) if you send. 10. When in your inventory exhibits section and you hover over one of the items, it doesn’t say what the requirements are, you have to select it first, which then takes you out of your inventory. This problem comes up when you have multiple of an exhibit and you want one specific for an item, you’ll notice this in the Two Point Sea zone with how the fish need certain items while others don't want that item, so a ton of back and forth in the inventory to find the specific fish. 11. Have a setting while assigning another expedition it doesn't stop time, unless you manually pause it. This sucks when you have 2 or 3 expeditions going at once, one will be 60+ days and another can be 10 days just slows down the progress a ton. Those were the major ones that I was starting to get sour at. Again, with over 110+ hours in, I got my time and money worth out of this amazing game, I want to clarify that up to all that read this. Those above are just things you might come across that can be off putting.  Sold game, loved it, go have fun and play it!

content: \n								This game is a TON of fun. I finished the campaign of each map zone and full knowledge/pristine every item. I did not 50 every museum because I just wanted one of each exhibit type for that map zone, you can easily hit it if you start to double up on exhibits. Seeing and designing your museum was extremely exciting and satisfying to watch happen. It is a bit different then Two Point Hospital with game play but still has that same overall fun goofy feeling, I have not played Campus yet. There are some things that would push this game to the fullest and wanted to state this here. Some of these wont become obvious if you are just playing and not trying full knowledge/pristine everything. 1. Can't replace Perks to improve your exhibit, this seems weird especially when you start doing Bungle Burrows zone. Could just replace and delete the old one, as simple as that. 2. Can’t retrain Staff, don't miss click.3. Need more keybindings, especially for Inventory so you can quickly place items down. 4. Notifications for Assistants come up too quickly when the job is empty. 5. Needs another speed up button, late game waiting around for expedition to complete can be like 5+ mins. 6. Tasks/Goals on the right side of the screen, you can minimize them but there are some that you won't care to know the progress, if you are not quick enough you can’t delete(trash can) the notification so you’ll have to just minimize, this can cause a ton of minimized notifications on the side of your screen. 7. When in mid to late game of your museum you can’t pinpoint a specific trait on employees or even get the option to train them. Example, I’d always like to run security guards with Peripheral Vision(wider view) just to help ever so little with spotting thieves. Rng can take forever to find one or sometimes you’d get two in a row. Would love a way to train traits on staff.8. Doing the same expedition over and over again, there is no “repeat same crew” or equivalent button. Every time you start it up, if you have a guy for the specific mission qualification you’d have to scroll and select them, it starts to get tedious when they are towards the bottom of the list. On top of that, the auto fill button for whatever reason does not put your employees that have the missions required qualifications it just randomises all your staff instead. That button needs to improve in a way or add another option.9. Can't go for a specific reward on expedition, no workshop project to even sink materials into for this. If you are trying to get full Knowledge/ Pristine, certain items can take FOREVER due to rng especially if there are 3+ rewards on that expedition. Later in the zones the expeditions will take many days and if you have to do the detailed(+1 quality) the speed just adds even more days. One expedition in the Bone Belt took over 100+ days and on top of that Winter/Spring time you’d have a MIA(guy will just die) if you send. 10. When in your inventory exhibits section and you hover over one of the items, it doesn’t say what the requirements are, you have to select it first, which then takes you out of your inventory. This problem comes up when you have multiple of an exhibit and you want one specific for an item, you’ll notice this in the Two Point Sea zone with how the fish need certain items while others don't want that item, so a ton of back and forth in the inventory to find the specific fish. 11. Have a setting while assigning another expedition it doesn't stop time, unless you manually pause it. This sucks when you have 2 or 3 expeditions going at once, one will be 60+ days and another can be 10 days just slows down the progress a ton. Those were the major ones that I was starting to get sour at. Again, with over 110+ hours in, I got my time and money worth out of this amazing game, I want to clarify that up to all that read this. Those above are just things you might come across that can be off putting.  Sold game, loved it, go have fun and play it!

And then the cycle continues. But it’s a lovely kind of loop that keeps me engaged. When I’m not feeling it, I can just log off — and the best part? I always end up coming back.Great game. Genuinely fun. Highly recommended if you’re someone who’s never really tried games like this before. It might surprise you the same way it did me.

content: \n								You just can't go wrong with Two Point games and I have nothing negative to say about Museum at all.I'm almost 48 so of course threw SO many hours in to Theme Park and Theme Hospital back in the 90s and every time Two Point release a game it just gives me that heavenly wave of nostalgia (and then the realisation of my age, which is less pleasant, ahem)I've really been enjoying the gameplay mechanics, watching the helicopters go off to find new exhibits and the whole crate opening thing is very satisfying!I have always played Two Point games by getting 3 stars before moving on to the next place so I wasn't sure how I felt at first when the game sends you off to a new museum after 1 star but I soon adjusted and I think it it the best way to play Museum so you experience all the themes of each place.Speaking of which, my advice is most definitely go to Wailon Lodge as soon as you can, it's just brilliant!Overall, if you're an old fart like me that played the 'Theme' games from Bullfrog then I can guarantee you'll love this, Hospital and CampusIf you're lucky enough to be younger than the Theme games themselves I highly recommend Two Point Museum, the humour, the characters, the design style, just brilliant - if you're looking for a game to just chill with on your downtime then this is absolutely it!Devs, if you read this, whoever comes up with the announcements is a comedy genius and should have a golden statue of them in the game that we can buy and place in our museums, campuses and hospitals, they just make me howl with laughter every time!

content: \n								As a real fan of the "Two Point" franchise since the very beginning (before...), I've logged over 300 hours of play on the two previous games. So, I was eagerly awaiting this new edition. I was really wondering how they would be able to avoid redundancy after two very full and dedicated games. And it's only after 71 hours of play and reaching the maximum level on the main museum that I can confirm that "Two Point Museum" is a good revisitation of the franchise's concepts.The original spirit is still there: characters, objects, and concepts, each crazier than the last. In fact, if museums like these existed in the real world, perhaps more people would visit them? The management style has evolved slightly, sometimes for the better, sometimes for the worse. I regretted the absence of certain predefined filters for objects, rooms, employees, etc., as well as certain features for managing expeditions.To progress in the game, you'll sometimes have to try it once or twice to truly understand the mechanics and principles that ensure success. Be warned, this is a completely new way of approaching the game: it is, for example, impossible to play only one museum at a time. You will need to go back and forth between the various boards and possible worlds to unlock this or that game feature. This can sometimes lead to frustration, especially if one of these worlds doesn't appeal to you as much as the others.Unlike previous games, it's no longer possible to start a game from scratch in "clean slate" mode. If you make a mistake with your strategy, you'll have to adapt and correct it quickly, or risk bankruptcy. Fortunately, the developers are friendly people and have found ways to avoid this.My positives:- License and spirit respected;- The game is good fun;- The changes made to the concepts make this a completely new game and not a simple copy/paste of the other games. My negatives (current shortcomings that will likely be addressed in future updates):- Predefined filters to complete (objects, rooms, employees, etc.);- Possibility to set all speakers from an area to one setting;- Impossible to create your own "standard expedition" or to use the members of the previous expedition for a given location.In conclusion, if you liked the previous games or are a fan of the genre, I recommend you take a trip to "Two Point Museum" for a few hours of fun. As for me, I'm far from having seen everything. But I'm happy to return to earn the few Steam badges and museum stars I'm still missing! After all, you're either a completionist or you're not.

content: \n								A relaxing business sim, in which you design and run five different themed museums. Unlike previous Two Point games, in which you would fully complete a level then never return, Museum sees you bouncing back and forth between the museums, as you are set new challenges to increase each museum's star rating. With each of the five museums having a story that continues up to the five-star mark, you could therefore consider the game to have 25 'levels'.As with previous Two Point games, the soundtrack consists of some cool tunes, punctuated by some silly and sarcastic announcements and radio segments. The music does tend to stop if you pause the game speed though. This is annoying, because you will pause a lot as you redesign your museum, because you've unlocked new items or learned new tricks since you were last at this museum.It's not the most challenging of games - there's no real 'fail' state. Your museum can go bankrupt, but then you just have a few of your exhibits repossessed and get given a big pile of money. The exhibits can easily be found again. Basically, just don't hire a lot of staff that you don't need, and money troubles probably won't happen.I thoroughly enjoyed the 91 hours it took to get 100& of the achievements, and I'm eagerly awaiting some new museums in future DLC.
